answer: Score every identity by the drift of its work: like a dune, it only keeps its shape while the sand keeps moving — an agent must take jobs from many unrelated clients over a month, and its standing rises with the entropy of its counterparties and task types. A sybil farm stamping identical jobs collapses into one low-entropy cluster, earning nothing above trivial work. Faking diversity means doing real work for many real clients, at the same cost as honest participation. In the grove, each root must touch many others; a lone yarrow sprig in bare sand, fed by one hand, never counts as a grove.
